transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Olivia (Redwood CSM), Mark (Verdance Head Eng), Priya (Platform Lead), Ben (Ops), Sarah (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align pilot goals and security posture. A few decisions but mostly intake and action items.

[00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros, I'll kick it off. I'm Jasmine Patel, AE here at Redwood.
[00:15] Mark: Hey, Mark Reyes, head of eng at Verdance. Thanks. We've got Priya and Ben here, and Sarah from procurement joining shortly.
[00:30] Priya: Hi, Priya Kapoor, platform lead.
[00:36] Ben: Ben Ortiz, ops.
[00:42] Sarah: Sarah Liu, procurement. Sorry I'm a couple minutes late.
[00:48] Jasmine: No worries, great. Goal for today's session is to finalize pilot scope and capture network/security constraints so Liam and Olivia can stand up the pilot. We'll also list acceptance criteria and timeline.
[01:10] Olivia: I'll drop the onboarding runbook and our SOC2 pack after the call. Expect a network diagram and a list of artifacts.
[01:25] Mark: High level we want to validate both latency and cost tradeoffs. We currently run a transformer-based reranker in-house and want inference for a mix of reranking and chat generation. Target is p95 under 120ms for the reranker route, and p95 under 800ms for longer generation.
[01:50] Liam: Got it. For reranking, we usually recommend keeping the model small and using KV cache optimizations; we'll propose a quantized variant and a batch policy.
[02:10] Priya: Network wise, we need to know if we can use Redwood's hosted API or if we have to go VPC/private. Data is moderately sensitive; PHI isn't in scope but customer PII rules apply, so we may need dedicated VPC.
[02:35] Olivia: We support both hosted and Redwood Private (VPC). For private deployments we provide a private control plane plus KMS integration. We'll share the differences in the pack.
[02:52] Mark: Regarding KMS, we use an HSM-backed KMS; are there compatibility notes?
[03:05] Liam: Yes we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers. We had one customer who used an external HSM via a gateway—some extra network setup was required but it's supported. We'll include steps.
[03:28] Priya: Any hard dependencies on specific networking ports? We have strict egress rules.
[03:36] Liam: We'll provide an allowlist. Usually TLS on 443 plus a handful of internal service ports for health checks if you do a private deployment. We'll list exact CIDR ranges.
[03:55] Ben: How about data retention? We need logs for six months for audit.
[04:03] Olivia: Audit logs are configurable; we can push logs into your SIEM or provide log exports. Retention can be extended as an add-on.
[04:20] Mark: Pilot scope — what duration are you proposing?
[04:26] Jasmine: Typical pilot is 30 days with a capped token budget for the pilot. For this engagement let's propose 30 days, up to 100k tokens/day to validate performance and stability. If you need longer, we can extend.
[04:45] Priya: That sounds fine, but we need to run some spike tests to simulate Black Friday-like spikes.
[04:54] Liam: We can run synthetic spike tests. We'll configure a load profile and run a stress test. For performance expectations, do you have expected concurrency and avg tokens per request?
[05:10] Priya: Avg 3-12 tokens for reranker, 150-600 tokens for generation, concurrency up to 60 concurrent requests during spikes.
[05:24] Liam: Ok that's helpful. We'll size the pilot accordingly and propose autoscaling thresholds.
[05:38] Mark: On the SLA — we need 99.5% availability during trading hours and an incident escalation path.
[05:47] Olivia: Our default SLA for Dedicated customers matches that. For Hosted we offer best-effort but can provide SLOs and escalation playbooks.
[06:00] Sarah: Procurement wondering about contract length and pilot terms; can we run a no-cost pilot?
[06:08] Jasmine: We typically run a short pilot with a small install fee to cover reserved capacity for the load test. Sometimes we credit that against the first month. We'll share a pilot contract template.
[06:22] Sarah: Great, please send the template so legal can review.
[06:28] Priya: On observability, we need token-level cost visibility and per-route latency dashboards. Is that available?
[06:38] Olivia: Yes, Redwood Console provides token/route breakdowns, tracing hooks, and per-model dashboards. We'll include a demo link in the pack.
[06:52] Mark: Any vendor lock-in concerns? We want the ability to move workloads if needed.
[06:58] Liam: We keep model artifacts portable and support standard formats; you can pin model versions. For dedicated/private you own the data and keys; we provide export mechanisms.
[07:15] Priya: What about fallback behavior if capacity is exhausted? We need graceful degradation.
[07:22] Liam: We can set routing fallback to a cheaper model variant or to degraded throughput with a response header indicating fallback. We'll show options.
[07:36] Mark: Perf question — can we run one of our real payloads through a bench?
[07:42] Liam: Yes, if you can share an anonymized sample we can run it in the pilot. We'll need csv/json with prompts and target shapes.
[07:55] Priya: We'll prepare that. Expect to send it by 12/07.
[08:02] Jasmine: Good. Let's capture acceptance criteria: 1) Reranker p95 < 120ms; 2) Generation p95 < 800ms for 90% of sample prompts; 3) No data exfiltration incidents; 4) Operational dashboards reporting costs and latency. Any additions?
[08:28] Mark: Add load stability during 2x spike.
[08:33] Ben: And a recovery time objective for incidents — say RTO < 30m for critical incidents.
[08:40] Olivia: Noted. We'll propose incident playbooks and runbooks.
[08:49] Sarah: From procurement side, we need liability clauses and data handling language. I'll review the pilot contract when you send it.
[08:58] Jasmine: We'll include sample terms; pilot contract is standard but flexible for enterprise redlines.
[09:06] Priya: A few technical deep-dive items — quantization approach, kernel selection, and batching policies. Liam, can you cover those?
[09:16] Liam: Sure. For quantization we'll typically use 4-bit or 8-bit where tolerable, depends on model quality tolerances. Kernel selection is automatic in our runtime but we can pin kernels for reproducibility. Batching: continuous batching helps throughput but increases tail latency; we'll tune thresholds to meet p95.
[09:40] Mark: Will quantization affect answer quality?
[09:44] Liam: Slightly; we'll baseline with your prompts. If quality degrades beyond an agreed delta, we'll try alternate strategies like KV caching and model distillation.
[09:58] Priya: Any limitations around private deployment on-prem?
[10:04] Olivia: On-prem has an additional ops footprint; we provide an on-prem package that requires access to your cluster, and we can integrate with local KMS. For your use-case, VPC is likely a better first step.
[10:20] Mark: Cost modeling — can you show a rough per-token cost for the pilot?
[10:26] Jasmine: We'll send a cost model after we size infra from the perf tests. Roughly, dedicated deployment lowers unit cost but has commit fees. Hosted is pay-as-you-go.
[10:36] Sarah: Procurement will review once we have a written estimate.
[10:41] Olivia: I'll attach a sample cost spreadsheet and an example rollout plan.
[10:48] Mark: Timeline — we want go/no-go decision by mid-January for a phased roll in late Jan. Is that feasible?
[10:55] Jasmine: Yes, it fits. Pilot in December, dry-run early Jan, go-live window later in Jan.
[11:05] Priya: Ok, let's lock the pilot start for Dec 13 so we can get results before the holidays.
[11:11] Liam: Works—we'll aim to have pilot env provisioned within 5 business days after we get the sample payload and signed pilot agreement.
[11:21] Jasmine: Any other blockers?
[11:25] Ben: None from ops aside from CIDR ranges.
[11:29] Sarah: Procurement needs the contract and SLA to start review.
[11:33] Mark: We're good to proceed on the technical side.
[11:38] Olivia: I'll follow up with the security pack and runbook, Jasmine will share contract template, Liam will schedule perf runs.
[11:46] Jasmine: Great. Recap of next steps and action owners live in the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
[11:55] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript contains some ASR artifacts (proper nouns sometimes mistranscribed), and speaker turns were consolidated for readability.
